name: Clean strategic answer: applied framework, trade-offs, metrics, stakeholders, risks

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: How would you grow Razorpay into the SMB segment? What would you NOT do?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Applied to Razorpay specifically: SMBs care about onboarding speed and pricing transparency, not feature breadth. Strength is our existing developer trust. So I'd build a self-serve onboarding flow targeting <100-employee firms in tier-2 cities. The trade-off is we'd deprioritize enterprise white-glove sales for two quarters — that's the opportunity cost. Stakeholders: the engineering team owns onboarding, sales team needs realignment, partners get a referral commission. Risk: competitors copy the flow within 6 months — mitigation is bundling our analytics. Success metric: 25% increase in <100-employee accounts in 2 quarters, with onboarding time below 10 minutes.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I would not pursue regulated industries this year — KYC overhead would slow shipping. And I would not lower prices below 1.5% — it signals desperation and trains customers wrong. The opportunity cost of going low is permanent positioning damage.
